instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

entry = await rlm.harness.create_memory(title='Continual-ARC task-d5c2d8dd: count upright and inverted T tetrominoes into two 3x3 panels', path='arc/continual_arc', global_=True, content='''For recurrent task-d5c2d8dd, input is a sparse grid of color-2 T tetrominoes on background 0. Each object is a horizontal run of three 2s plus one centered stem cell immediately above or below. Count the two orientations separately and return a 3x6 grid split into two 3x3 panels. T with stem ABOVE its horizontal bar contributes to the LEFT panel, color 3. T with stem BELOW its bar contributes to the RIGHT panel, color 1. For each panel, encode count n using corner cells in this order: local (row 0,col 0), (row 2,col 0), (row 0,col 2), (row 2,col 2), all other cells 0. Thus n=1 marks upper-left; n=2 marks upper-left and lower-left; n=3 adds upper-right; n=4 marks all four corners. Colors are 3 in the left panel (columns 0..2) and 1 in the right panel (columns 3..5). Demos validate: demo with one T of each orientation outputs 3 at [0,0], 1 at [0,3]; demo with 2 stem-above and 1 stem-below outputs 3 at left upper-left and lower-left, 1 at right upper-left; demo with 3 stem-above and 4 stem-below outputs count-3 pattern in left and all four corners in right. Current accepted test had 2 stem-above and 3 stem-below, yielding [[3,0,0,1,0,1],[0,0,0,0,0,0],[3,0,0,1,0,0]]. Ensure count each disconnected T once and observe output dimensions 3x6, not the input size.''')
print(entry)
